rows.title: There Will Be Flood
rows.standfirst: Windell Curole spent decades working to protect his community in southern Louisiana from the destructive flooding caused by hurricanes. His local office in South Lafourche partnered with the federal government's Army Corps of Engineers to build a massive ring of earthen mounds – also known as levees – to keep the floodwaters at bay.

rows.title: A company that turned homeowners into renters abruptly shuts down
rows.standfirst: EasyKnock, which pioneered 'sale-leaseback' deals for struggling homeowners, abruptly closes its doors

rows.title: This little electric car made history. 25 years ago, GM stopped making it
rows.standfirst: The EV1 was the first modern, mass-produced electric vehicle from a major automaker — pioneering some technologies you can still find in today's EVs. But the model was controversial, and short-lived.

rows.title: Men without college degrees aren't doing well
rows.standfirst: Many men in America don't feel like they're doing as well as their fathers. But what does the data say? Today on the show, we speak to Richard Reeves from the American Institute for Boys and Men about what's really going on with men's wages and what potential solutions could look like.

rows.title: Court upholds a U.S. ban on TikTok
rows.standfirst: TikTok has been facing down a January divest-or-be-banned deadline. The company filed a lawsuit challenging the law, which was heard before a federal appeals court in Washington, D.C.

rows.title: After a shocking shooting, Americans vent feelings about health insurance
rows.standfirst: The death of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson triggered a deluge of painful stories about health care denials on social media.

rows.title: Court rejects Boeing plea deal stemming from 737 Max crashes
rows.standfirst: A federal judge in Texas has rejected a plea deal between Boeing and the U.S. Justice Department, saying the court should play a bigger role in selecting an independent monitor to oversee the company.

rows.title: New images are released for a 'person of interest' in the CEO's killing in New York
rows.standfirst: Shell casings with the cryptic words "deny," "defend" and "depose" were found at the scene of the fatal shooting of the UnitedHealthcare CEO outside of a Manhattan hotel, police officials say.

rows.title: Anthem reverses plans to put time limits on anesthesia coverage
rows.standfirst: Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield was under scrutiny for planning to put time limits on anesthesia care. On Thursday, the large health insurer said it had decided not to proceed with the policy change.

rows.title: Pantone's 2025 color is Mocha Mousse: How the company sold color to the world
rows.standfirst: Pantone isn't the only color system of its kind. But thanks to an innovative founder and savvy marketing, it's become the industry standard.

rows.title: What a second Trump term could mean for SpaceX
rows.standfirst: SpaceX is capping off a busy 2024, with more than 100 rocket launches, including its vaunted Starship. NPR Science Correspondent Geoff Brumfiel attended the November launch of Starship alongside SpaceX founder Elon Musk and president-elect Donald Trump. He spoke with NPR's Short Wave about the environmental impact of these launches in south Texas — and what a second Trump administration could mean for the company.

rows.title: Bitcoin hits $100,000 for the first time. 3 things to know about an incredible ride
rows.standfirst: From how it got here to why critics are alarmed, here's what to know about the spectacular milestone for bitcoin.

rows.title: Trump picks crypto backer Paul Atkins as new Securities and Exchange Commission chair
rows.standfirst: Trump picked Atkins, a former SEC commissioner, to head the agency. Known for his support of cryptocurrencies, Atkins could help shape regulations for the industry.

rows.title: Who is Brian Thompson, the UnitedHealthcare CEO gunned down in New York?
rows.standfirst: Thompson, a 50-year-old father of two, spent two decades at UnitedHealth Group before his shocking death. Tributes are pouring in from coworkers and public officials in his home state of Minnesota.

rows.title: Nearly 500 journalists walk out at 'The Guardian' and its sister paper
rows.standfirst: Nearly 500 journalists have walked out of the Guardian and its sister paper, the Observer, to protest what they see as a betrayal of the paper's values: the planned sale of the Observer to a startup.

rows.title: ABC agrees to give $15 million to Trump's presidential library to settle lawsuit
rows.standfirst: ABC News agreed to pay $15 million to Trump's presidential library to settle a lawsuit over George Stephanopoulos' inaccurate on-air assertion that Trump was found liable for raping E. Jean Carroll.

rows.title: A Nobel prize for explaining why there's global inequality
rows.standfirst: Why do some nations fail and others succeed?

rows.title: McKinsey & Company to pay $650 million for role in opioid crisis
rows.standfirst: The powerful consulting firm McKinsey will "accept responsibility" and pay $650 million for helping to fuel the opioid crisis, but executives will once again dodge prosecution.

rows.title: Tech moguls Altman, Bezos and Zuckerberg donate to Trump's inauguration fund
rows.standfirst: The donations are seen as the latest example of tech moguls' changing stance toward the incoming president. During his first administration, Trump clashed with Bezos and Zuckerberg.

rows.title: Here are the deadlines for mailing your holiday gifts to ensure they arrive on time
rows.standfirst: Mail carriers and shipping companies will be closed on Christmas Day.

rows.title: How D.C. tackled a child care crunch through a tax hike on the rich
rows.standfirst: In Washington, D.C., a tax on residents earning more than $250,000 a year is boosting the wages of child care workers. Two years in, it's proving to be a great investment.

rows.title: A supermarket beef, a quantum leap, and Christmas trees for cheap
rows.standfirst: It's the most wonderful time of year, er, week, because it's that time when we look at the most fascinating economic numbers from the news.

rows.title: Stanley recalls about 2.6 million travel mugs
rows.standfirst: The company behind the uber-viral water bottles is recommending customers affected by the recall reach out for a replacement part.

rows.title: Trump says Kari Lake will lead Voice of America. He attacked it during his first term
rows.standfirst: If successful, Trump's move would install a loyalist at the helm of the network. A U.S. judge found Trump appointees illegally violated Voice of America's journalistic independence in his first term.

rows.title: Budget airlines are struggling. Their solution? Go upscale
rows.standfirst: NPR's A Martinez talks to Kyle Potter of Thrifty Traveler, about what the change says about the future of flying on the cheap.

rows.title: An economist's role in the fall of Syria's government
rows.standfirst: In 2012, Karam Shaar had to leave his home country of Syria due to the civil war. But he still wanted to make a difference. Through his economic analysis, he uncovered concerning patterns about how the Assad regime and its cronies were siphoning money from humanitarian aid. Today on the show, the story of how one Syrian exile contributed to the resistance while on the other side of the world.

rows.title: Albertsons sues Kroger and ends failed grocery megamerger
rows.standfirst: The lawsuit over a deal to combine the two largest U.S. supermarkets came just a day after it was blocked in both federal and Washington state courts.

rows.title: Worst. Tariffs. Ever. (update)
rows.standfirst: The Smoot Hawley Tariffs were a debacle that helped plunge America into the Great Depression. What can we learn from them?

rows.title: The brewing recovery in Western North Carolina
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve's last Beige Book of 2024 is like Spotify Wrapped but for the economy. There's a little bit of everything inside — labor markets, inflation and even natural disasters. On today's show, we spotlight Western North Carolina's challenging recovery after Hurricane Helene, and check in with an Asheville malt manufacturer on the impact to local businesses.

rows.title: GM to retreat from robotaxis and stop funding its Cruise autonomous vehicle unit
rows.standfirst: The automaker will focus on development of partially automated driver-assist systems for personal vehicles like its Super Cruise, which allows drivers to take their hands off the steering wheel.

rows.title: Party City files for bankruptcy and plans to shutter nationwide
rows.standfirst: Party City was once unmatched in its vast selection of affordable celebration goods. But over the years, competition stacked up at Walmart, Target, Spirit Halloween, and especially Amazon.

rows.title: Netflix is dreaming of a glitch-free Christmas with 2 major NFL games set
rows.standfirst: It comes weeks after Netflix's attempt to broadcast live boxing between Jake Paul and Mike Tyson was rife with technical glitches.

rows.title: The habitat banker
rows.standfirst: Our planet is in serious trouble. There are a million species of plants and animals in danger of extinction, and the biggest cause is companies destroying their habitats to farm food, mine minerals, and otherwise get the raw materials to turn into the products we all consume.

rows.title: What a government shutdown could mean for your holiday travel plans
rows.standfirst: Millions of Americans are planning to travel in the coming days. Here's what a potential government shutdown could mean for flying, driving and more — and what you can do to prepare.

rows.title: In a lawsuit, CFPB says 3 top U.S. banks failed to protect consumers from Zelle fraud
rows.standfirst: The consumer financial watchdog says customers of the top three banks lost more than $870 million over seven years due to a lack of safeguards against fraud on the Zelle network.

rows.title: GOP stop-gap bill fails, bringing potential shutdown closer. And, NPR's guide to dance
rows.standfirst: Congress has until midnight tonight to avoid a government shutdown after House Republicans were unable to pass a stop-gap funding bill yesterday. And, tips to improve your dance moves.

rows.title: Starbucks workers say they will begin a strike in 3 cities on Friday
rows.standfirst: Starbucks and Starbucks Workers United said in February they had come to common ground in moving forward for the rest of the year. But the union says Starbucks has not kept its end of the commitment.

rows.title: Big Lots says it is having going-out-of-business sales as it seeks a new buyer
rows.standfirst: The national discount retailer says that a previously announced deal to sell itself to a private-equity group fell through.

rows.title: Trump is all about tariffs as he leads a party that used to be all about free trade
rows.standfirst: Once upon a time, Republicans spoke of free trade in glowing terms. With his constant threats of tariffs and a history of implementing them, President-elect Donald Trump has flipped that on its head.

rows.title: Big Health Care is ending a terrible year. Is anyone happy with this business?
rows.standfirst: Patients are protesting, bipartisan lawmakers are threatening regulation – and investors are selling their shares.

rows.title: Help us pick the indicator of the year!
rows.standfirst: 2024 was a wild year for the U.S. economy: The economy did well in terms of inflation and unemployment, but vibes ruled the roost. (Mostly didn't feel great!) Additionally, Bitcoin went to the moon and some wacky stuff was happening with unemployment and job opening rates, showing that we might have achieved an economic soft landing.

rows.title: How will Australia's under-16 social media ban work? We asked the law's enforcer
rows.standfirst: Australia's top online internet regulator explains how the nation plans to roll out the world's first social media ban for kids under 16.

rows.title: Possible government shutdown looms. And, tips to help with seasonal depression
rows.standfirst: Possible holiday government shutdown looms as President-elect Donald Trump and advisers like Elon Musk object to bipartisan spending bill. And, simple ways to help with seasonal depression.

rows.title: Amazon faces multiple pickets as union targets holiday shopping rush
rows.standfirst: The Teamsters union demands that Amazon recognize its unionized workers. The company refuses and says the strikes won't affect operations.

rows.title: Can empty-nesters boost housing affordability?
rows.standfirst: The "silver tsunami" of aging Americans is often seen as a potential way to alleviate the country's housing affordability woes. However, the data suggests that an influx of empty-nester homes coming on the market won't have much of an impact on the problem—because of a geographical mismatch.

rows.title: The curious rise of novelty popcorn buckets (Encore)
rows.standfirst: Even before the Dune: Part 2 popcorn bucket went viral this year, movie theaters have been trying all types of ways to lure customers back. There's reclining seats, expanded menu options, and even more merchandise. Today on the show, we track the rise of the popcorn bucket and its afterlife on eBay.

rows.title: South Korea to inspect Boeing aircraft as it struggles to find cause of plane crash
rows.standfirst: Many worry how effectively the South Korean government will handle the disaster as it grapples with a leadership vacuum after the impeachments of the country's top two officials.

rows.title: Invest like a Congress member (Encore)
rows.standfirst: There are some new funds that track stock trading by members of Congress and their family. So we thought, why don't we get in on that?

rows.title: Big Lots reaches deal to keep hundreds of U.S. stores open
rows.standfirst: Big Lots said Friday it will be sold to Gordon Brothers Retail Partners, a firm that specializes in distressed companies.

rows.title: Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen says U.S. could hit debt limit in weeks
rows.standfirst: Yellen told Congress her agency will need to start taking "extraordinary measures," or special accounting maneuvers intended to prevent the nation from hitting the debt ceiling, as early as Jan. 14.

rows.title: Trump asks the Supreme Court to delay the start of the TikTok ban
rows.standfirst: President-elect Donald Trump asked the Supreme Court on Friday to pause the potential TikTok ban from going into effect until his administration can pursue a "political resolution" to the issue.

rows.title: Sportscaster Greg Gumbel dies at age 78
rows.standfirst: Greg Gumbel, a longtime CBS sportscaster, has died from cancer, according to a statement from family released by CBS on Friday. He was 78.

rows.title: The Rest of the Story, 2024
rows.standfirst: After the gift exchange comes another great holiday tradition: returns season. Once again, we are joining the fun in our own Planet Money way. We are returning to stories from years past to see what's changed since we last reported them. It's an episode we call The Rest of the Story.

rows.title: Claim of dementia could derail former Abercrombie CEO's sex trafficking case
rows.standfirst: Can his legal team's claims that he has late-onset Alzheimer's disease and dementia put a pause in the sex trafficking trial of former Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Mike Jeffries?

rows.title: Delta apologizes — again — after another stowaway boards a flight without ticket
rows.standfirst: The incident marks the second time in less than a month that an unticketed passenger was discovered on a Delta Air Lines flight, this time en route to Hawaii.

rows.title: Top global TikToks in 2024: Mr. Bean disciple, lip-synch for their life, baby hippo!
rows.standfirst: Scenes from some of the most popular TikToks from the Global South in 2024: a dancing teen from the Philippines; an homage to Mr. Bean, that cute baby pygmy hippo.

rows.title: Half a billion people need reading glasses. Why can't they get them? (Encore)
rows.standfirst: If you need some reading glasses in the United States, you don't have to break the bank to pick some up. That's important for older folks who need a little extra magnification. But in some parts of the world, people who need readers don't have that privilege. Today on the show, we'll find out why that is and learn the economic solution to the reading glasses shortage.

rows.title: Richard Parsons, who steadied Time Warner and Citigroup, dies at 76
rows.standfirst: Parsons, one of corporate America's most prominent Black executives who held top posts at Time Warner and Citigroup, was known as a skilled negotiator, a diplomat and a crisis manager.

rows.title: The 'Beyoncé Bowl' halftime show was a massive hit for Netflix. The football was too
rows.standfirst: Netflix says more than 200 countries tuned into the "Beyoncé Bowl" and its two NFL games. We may just be starting to learn what that ultimately means for the future of television and sports media.

rows.title: Israeli strike kills 5 Palestinian journalists in Gaza, officials say
rows.standfirst: An Israeli strike killed five Palestinian journalists outside a hospital in the Gaza Strip overnight, according to the Health Ministry. The Israeli military said it had targeted a group of militants.

frame: Up to15 visible Business-archive cards at four fixed weekly endpoints, restricted to each block; not a full-publication census
